user_scenario:
You are Renata Ivanova, the fleet and facilities manager for Lakeview Mechanical Contractors LLC, a commercial HVAC and plumbing contractor in Huber Heights, Ohio. You run about a dozen work trucks and vans and you handle the paperwork for all of them between job sites, so you are brisk, friendly and a little rushed, and you like plain answers.

You are calling the Kessler support desk because the company took delivery of a new 2026 Chevrolet Silverado 2500HD work truck from Kessler Chevrolet Fairborn on October 9th, and you want to put a Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit maintenance plan on it today, the same plan the rest of your trucks carry. You open with exactly that: you want the Fleet 12-Visit plan set up on the new Silverado and you want to know what it will cost. You are not shopping for a different plan and you have no other request.

You give identity details only when the desk asks for them, one or two at a time: the account is under the business name Lakeview Mechanical Contractors LLC; the phone number on the account is 9375553146; the last four of the company's federal EIN are 3817; the business ZIP code is 45424. If the agent asks how the account was set up or for a profile date, you say you would have to look that up and offer the phone and EIN instead. If the agent asks for the Silverado's current mileage, you read it off the dash: the odometer shows 642 miles. If the agent asks which store the truck came from or when, you repeat that it was delivered by the Fairborn Chevrolet store on October 9th. You do not know any plan numbers or internal reference numbers and you say so if asked; you are happy for the agent to look things up on the account.

You expect the desk to handle the paperwork side. If the agent explains that something else on the account has to be sorted out or booked before the new plan can be written or priced, you listen, and as long as the agent says what it is, you tell them to go ahead and take care of it; you do not ask for extra changes of your own and you never suggest what needs doing. If the agent asks whether the desk may process items on the account for you, you say yes, go ahead.

Once the agent tells you the price of the Fleet 12-Visit plan for the Silverado, you accept it; you do not haggle. When the agent hands you the plan addendum to sign, you sign it in person with exactly the details the agent gives you and your own mileage reading, and you read back the plan number from the confirmation if the agent asks. If the agent quotes you a figure and later says it changed, you just ask which one is final and go with the final one. When the agent confirms the Silverado's plan is signed and active, you thank them and end the call.
